column1: Why use Query Store instead of relying only on cached-plan statistics?
column2:
It retains query and plan performance history across cache eviction.
Its history is database-persisted but remains subject to capture and retention policies.
Review source

column1: How does Query Store organize runtime execution statistics?
column2:
Aggregates per plan over configurable time intervals.
It writes data asynchronously rather than storing a separate runtime record for every execution.
Review source

column1: Which SSMS Query Store report identifies queries whose performance worsened between time periods?
column2:
Regressed Queries.
Compare the query's plans and metrics to investigate whether a plan change caused the regression.
Review source

column1: Which SSMS Query Store report finds the largest consumers of a selected resource over a time range?
column2:
Top Resource Consuming Queries.
Choose a metric and aggregation that match the performance problem.
Review source

column1: Which SSMS Query Store report highlights inconsistent query performance?
column2:
Queries With High Variation.
Large variation can indicate parameter sensitivity, but it does not prove that cause.
Review source

column1: What is the role of plan forcing when a new execution plan causes a regression?
column2:
Restore a previously good plan while investigating the root cause.
Monitor its performance and review it when the workload or data changes.
Review source

column1: What happens if Query Store cannot force a selected plan?
column2:
The optimizer optimizes the query normally.
Forcing requests the same or a similar plan, not a guarantee of identical execution or performance.
Review source

column1: Which Query Store feature applies query hints without changing application SQL?
column2:
Query Store hints.
Available in SQL Server 2022 and later, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and SQL database in Fabric.
Review source

column1: Which hints take precedence over hard-coded statement hints and plan guide hints?
column2:
Query Store hints.
They persist across restarts and failovers until removed or changed.
Review source

column1: What tradeoff does a Query Store RECOMPILE hint make?
column2:
A new plan for each execution at the cost of compilation CPU.
It can help parameter-sensitive queries but is not compatible with database forced parameterization.
Review source

column1: What happens to an incompatible Query Store tuning hint that would prevent a valid plan?
column2:
The engine ignores the hint and allows the query to execute.
Inspect sys.query_store_query_hints for failure details rather than assuming that the hint took effect.
Review source

column1: Which SSMS report links historical query waits to resource categories?
column2:
Query Wait Statistics.
Query Store groups related wait types into categories such as Lock, Buffer IO, CPU, and Memory.
Review source

column1: What do high Query Store Lock waits identify about a query?
column2:
It spends time waiting for locks.
The waiting query is not necessarily the blocker, so investigate other transactions touching the same data.
Review source

column1: Which Azure portal feature visualizes Query Store resource-consumption history for Azure SQL Database?
column2:
Query Performance Insight (QPI).
Query Store must be active and must capture workload data before useful charts appear.
Review source

column1: Why can QPI omit queries that collectively consume much of the database's resources?
column2:
It displays only the selected top 5 to 20 queries.
Use Query Store catalog views or SSMS to investigate beyond the displayed subset.
Review source

column1: Which catalog view shows Query Store's actual state, requested state, and storage usage?
column2:
sys.database_query_store_options.
Compare actual_state_desc with desired_state_desc and examine readonly_reason if collection stops.
Review source

column1: How do you restore Query Store collection after its storage quota is reached in Azure SQL Database?
column2:
Increase its quota or remove unneeded history, then restore READ_WRITE mode.
Confirm the cause first because other conditions can also force READ_ONLY mode.
Review source

column1: What does Query Store's AUTO capture mode prioritize?
column2:
Queries selected by execution frequency and resource consumption.
This reduces storage spent on infrequent, negligible-cost queries.
Review source

column1: What does Query Store's automatic size-based cleanup do?
column2:
Removes less expensive and older queries as storage approaches its quota.
Time-based retention separately controls how long stale query information remains.
Review source

column1: Why weight Query Store interval averages by count_executions when combining durations?
column2:
Intervals can contain different execution counts.
Use SUM(avg_duration * count_executions) / NULLIF(SUM(count_executions), 0), not AVG(avg_duration).
Review source

column1: Why does filtering Query Store rows by last_execution_time not produce an exact last-hour execution sample?
column2:
Each matching row aggregates an interval that can cross the cutoff.
The filter selects interval summaries, not individual executions within the requested hour.
Review source
